description: The Galileo Reference Antenna Pattern (GRAP) is a statistical model of how the transmit power of the Galileo full operational capability satellites varies with direction, including side lobes, built from the measurements of the antenna characterisation campaign. The 2024 paper by the Joint Research Centre explains the reconstruction procedure, based on antenna characterisation techniques and statistical learning, analyses its resolution, smoothness and statistical distribution, and adds a use case in which a new indicator called accessibility summarises the expected Galileo signal quality for different orbital altitudes and mission requirements in the space service volume. Producer: the European Commission Joint Research Centre, published in Sensors in March 2024. Coverage: the Galileo constellation, for space users at high orbits. Access: the paper is open access on PubMed Central; no downloadable pattern files were seen on the page read. Licence and cost: free; the article states CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the model is described in the paper and its numerical files are not linked here, and the approach is extended to other systems only as a possibility. Simulation uses: the pattern feeds analyses of GNSS signal availability and navigation performance for satellites in high orbits. Related records: Galileo constellation status (data-galileo-constellation-status) and Galileo satellite metadata (data-galileo-satellite-metadata).
